Given below are two statements :
**Statement-I**: When a capillary tube is dipped into a liquid, the liquid neither rises nor falls in the capillary. The contact angle may be $0^\circ$.
**Statement-II**: The contact angle between a solid and a liquid is a property of the material of the solid and liquid as well :
In the light of above statement, choose the **correct** answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
Capillary rise $h = \frac{2T\cos\theta}{\rho g r}$ ;
If $\theta = 0^\circ$ then rise is non-zero
$\therefore$ Statement-1 is incorrect.
Option(1) is correct

questions.stem:
Given below are two statements:
**Statement-I:** Figure shows the variation of stopping potential with frequency ($\nu$) for the two photosensitive materials $M_1$ and $M_2$. The slope gives value of $\frac{h}{e}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant, $e$ is the charge of electron.
**Statement-II:** $M_2$ will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy for the incident radiation having same frequency.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
$eV_{0} = h\nu - \phi$
$V_{0} = \frac{h}{e}\nu - \frac{\phi}{e}$
$M_2$ material has higher work function, so statement-(II) is incorrect.
Option (1) is correct.

questions.stem: The angle between vector $\vec{Q}$ and the resultant of $(2\vec{Q} + 2\vec{P})$ and $(2\vec{Q} - 2\vec{P})$ is:
questions.solution:
$\vec{R} = (2\vec{Q} + 2\vec{P}) + (2\vec{Q} - 2\vec{P})$
$\vec{R} = 4\vec{Q}$
Angle between $\vec{Q}$ and $\vec{R}$ is zero
Option (1) is correct

If the collision frequency of hydrogen molecules in a closed chamber at $27^\circ$C is $Z$, then the collision frequency of the same system at $127^\circ$ C is :
questions.solution:
Assuming mean free path constant.
$f \propto v \propto \sqrt{T}$
$\frac{f_1}{f_2} = \sqrt{\frac{T_1}{T_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{300}{400}}$
$f_2 = \sqrt{\frac{4}{3}} f_1 = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}Z$

questions.stem: Time periods of oscillation of the same simple pendulum measured using four different measuring clocks were recorded as 4.62 s, 4.632 s, 4.6 s and 4.64 s. The arithmetic mean of these reading in correct significant figure is.
questions.solution:
Sum of number by considering significant digit
sum $= 4.6 + 4.6 + 4.6 + 4.6 = 18.4$
Arithmetic Mean $= \frac{sum}{4} = \frac{18.4}{4} = 4.6$

questions.stem: In the given figure $R_1 = 10\Omega$, $R_2 = 8\Omega$, $R_3 = 4\Omega$ and $R_4 = 8\Omega$. Battery is ideal with emf 12V. Equivalent resistant of the circuit and current supplied by the battery are respectively.
questions.solution:
Here $R_2, R_3, R_4$ are in parallel
$\frac{1}{R_{234}} = \frac{1}{R_2} + \frac{1}{R_3} + \frac{1}{R_4}$

questions.stem: An alternating voltage of amplitude 40 V and frequency 4 kHz is applied directly across the capacitor of 12 $\mu$F. The maximum displacement current between the plates of the capacitor is nearly:
questions.solution:
Displacement current is same as conduction current in capacitor.
$X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{2\pi f C}$
$= \frac{1}{2\pi\times4\times10^{3}\times12\times10^{-6}} = 3.317\Omega$
$I = \frac{V}{X_C} = \frac{40}{3.317} = 12\mathrm{A}$

If three helium nuclei combine to form a carbon nucleus then the energy released in this reaction is .......... $\times 10^{-2}$ MeV. (Given 1 u = 931 MeV/$c^{2}$, atomic mass of helium = 4.002603 u)
questions.solution:
Reaction :
$3\,{}_{2}^{4}\mathrm{He} \longrightarrow {}_{6}^{12}\mathrm{C} + \gamma$ rays
Mass defect $= \Delta m = (3m_{He} - m_C)$
$= (3\times4.002603 - 12) = 0.007809\ \mathrm{u}$
Energy released
$= 931\,\Delta m$ MeV
$= 7.27$ MeV $= 727\times10^{-2}$ MeV

questions.stem: An ac source is connected in given series LCR circuit. The rms potential difference across the capacitor of 20 $\mu$F is .............. V.
questions.solution:
$X_L = \omega L = 100\times1 = 100\Omega$
$X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{100\times20\times10^{-6}} = 500\Omega$
$Z = \sqrt{(X_L - X_C)^{2} + R^{2}}$
$\sqrt{(100-500)^{2} + 300^{2}}$
$Z = 500\Omega$
$i_{rms} = \frac{V_{rms}}{Z} = \frac{50}{500} = 0.1\mathrm{A}$
rms voltage across capacitor
$V_{rms} = X_C\, i_{rms}$
$= 500\times0.1 = 50\mathrm{V}$

questions.stem: In the experiment to determine the galvanometer resistance by half-deflection method, the plot of $\frac{1}{\theta}$ vs the resistance ($R$) of the resistance box is shown in the figure. The figure of merit of the galvanometer is .............. $\times10^{-1}$ A/division. [The source has emf 2V]

Three capacitors of capacitances 25 $\mu$F, 30 $\mu$F and 45 $\mu$F are connected in parallel to a supply of 100 V. Energy stored in the above combination is E. When these capacitors are connected in series to the same supply, the stored energy is $\frac{9}{x}E$. The value of $x$ is .................
questions.solution:
In parallel combination : Potential difference is same across all
Energy $= \frac{1}{2}(C_1 + C_2 + C_3)V^{2}$
$= \frac{1}{2}(25+30+45)\times(100)^{2}\times10^{-6} = 0.5 = E$
In series combination: Charge is same on all.
$\frac{1}{C_{equ}} = \frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_2} + \frac{1}{C_3} = \frac{1}{25} + \frac{1}{30} + \frac{1}{45}$
$\frac{1}{C_{equ}} = \frac{(18+15+10)}{450} = \frac{43}{450} \Rightarrow C_{equ} = \frac{450}{43}$
Energy $= \frac{Q^{2}}{2C_1} + \frac{Q^{2}}{2C_2} + \frac{Q^{2}}{2C_3}$
$= \frac{Q^{2}}{2}\left[\frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_2} + \frac{1}{C_3}\right]$
$\frac{(V\times C_{equ})^{2}}{2}\times\frac{1}{C_{equ}} = \frac{V^{2}C_{equ}}{2}$
$\frac{(100)^{2}}{2}\times\frac{450}{43}\times10^{-6}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{4.5}{86} = \frac{9}{x}E = \frac{9}{x}\times0.5 \Rightarrow x = 86$
